title: Sojourner Truth
summary: Born into slavery in New York as Isabella Baumfree, she became an itinerant preacher and changed her name to Sojourner Truth in 1843. She joined the antislavery and women's rights movements and spoke at the Woman's Rights Convention in Akron, Ohio, in May 1851. The best-known wording of that speech was published by Frances Gage in 1863. She died in Battle Creek, Michigan.

uncertainty.note: NPS gives 'circa 1797' for birth; Dickinson College's House Divided project says 'around 1797'.

where.modern_name: Akron, Summit County, Ohio (pinned to the 1851 Woman's Rights Convention; born in Ulster County, New York; died in Battle Creek, Michigan)
where.historical_name: Akron, Ohio, site of the Woman's Rights Convention, May 1851

importance.justification: Abolitionist and women's rights speaker whose 1851 Akron speech is one of the most cited of the era, though its popular wording is a later version.
